annotations.summary: Nginx web server unit failed

evidence: systemd_units probe: critical_failed_units=['nginx'] result=FAILED. `systemctl status nginx` → ActiveState=failed MainPID=0 SubState=dead. journalctl -u nginx --since '5 min ago' shows exit-code or signal.
root_cause: Systemd unit nginx transitioned to failed state. Root cause requires log inspection: OOM kill, config error, or dependency missing.

verification_steps.rationale: Last 50 log lines for failure reason
Check if a dependency failed first

proposed_remediation.step: systemctl restart nginx
If restart fails: journalctl -u nginx -n 100 to identify root cause before retry
If config error: validate config and reload — e.g., nginx -t / mysqld --validate-config

annotations.summary: Log partition disk full

evidence: disk_usage probe: critical_partitions=['/var/log(98%)'] result=FAILED. `df -h /var/log` → Use%=98% Avail=0.
root_cause: Log rotation failed or logging volume undersized.

proposed_remediation.step: find /var/log -name '*.log' -mtime +7 -delete (review first)
Increase partition size or add storage if growth is legitimate
Configure log rotation: logrotate -f /etc/logrotate.conf

annotations.summary: Inode exhaustion on spool partition

annotations.summary: NFS mount stale handle — I/O operations hanging

evidence: storage_nfs probe: nfs_error_count>0 stale_mounts=['/mnt/nfs-data'] result=FAILED. `stat /mnt/nfs-data` hangs or returns ESTALE. NFS server may be unreachable.
root_cause: NFS mount /mnt/nfs-data has stale handle or server connectivity issue. Processes waiting on I/O to this mount will block until remount or server recovery.

verification_steps.rationale: Verify NFS server exports are reachable

proposed_remediation.step: umount -l /mnt/nfs-data  # lazy unmount for stale handle
mount /mnt/nfs-data  # remount from fstab
If server unreachable: check NFS server health and network path

annotations.summary: MySQL max_connections hit — new connections refused

evidence: mysql_health probe: result=FAILED anomalies=[...]. threads_connected >= max_connections (151). New connection attempts fail with 'Too many connections'.
root_cause: Connection pool exhausted. Applications unable to connect. Queries queuing upstream.

proposed_remediation.step: Increase max_connections or reduce connection pool size in applications.

annotations.summary: MySQL replication SQL thread stopped — replica lag growing

evidence: mysql_health probe: result=FAILED anomalies=[...]. Slave_SQL_Running=No. Last_Error='Could not execute Write_rows_event'. Seconds_Behind_Master=3847.
root_cause: MySQL replication SQL thread stopped due to a row-format conflict or duplicate key. Replica data diverging from master.

proposed_remediation.step: STOP SLAVE; SET GLOBAL SQL_SLAVE_SKIP_COUNTER=1; START SLAVE; — only after confirming safe to skip.

annotations.summary: MySQL deadlock surge — transactions rolling back

evidence: mysql_health probe: result=FAILED anomalies=[...]. innodb_lock_waits=47 innodb_deadlocks_last_10min=38. Slow query log: 15 queries > 10s.
root_cause: Deadlock surge from concurrent transactions accessing same rows in different order. Applications see rollback errors.

proposed_remediation.step: Identify hot rows via SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS; restructure transaction order in application.

annotations.summary: ProxySQL client connection limit approaching — queries being queued

evidence: proxysql_health probe: result=FAILED anomalies=['proxysql_clients=1987>threshold']. ProxySQL Admin: SELECT * FROM stats_mysql_global WHERE Variable_Name='Client_Connections_connected' → 1987. mysql_connections_queued growing.
root_cause: ProxySQL client connection ceiling nearly reached. New connections are being queued or rejected depending on max_connections config.

verification_steps.command: mysql -h 127.0.0.1 -P 6032 -u radmin -pradmin -e "SELECT * FROM stats_mysql_global WHERE Variable_Name LIKE 'Client%'"

proposed_remediation.step: Reduce upstream application connection pool size to free ProxySQL slots
mysql -h 127.0.0.1 -P 6032 -u radmin -pradmin -e "SET mysql-max_connections=3000; SAVE MYSQL VARIABLES TO DISK; LOAD MYSQL VARIABLES TO RUNTIME"

annotations.summary: HAProxy backend app-backend has DOWN servers

evidence: service_haproxy probe: result=FAILED down_backends=['app-backend/server1', 'app-backend/server2']. `echo 'show stat' | socat stdio /var/run/haproxy/stats` → app-backend BACKEND=DOWN servers=2/2 DOWN.
root_cause: HAProxy backend 'app-backend' has servers in DOWN state. Health checks failing — upstream servers may be crashed, overloaded, or network-partitioned.

verification_steps.command: echo 'show stat' | socat stdio /var/run/haproxy/stats | cut -d',' -f1,2,18,19 | head -30
echo 'show info' | socat stdio /var/run/haproxy/stats | grep -i error

proposed_remediation.step: Check upstream servers in backend 'app-backend': ping, curl health endpoint, check service logs
If server is healthy but HAProxy marks it DOWN: verify health-check URI and interval config

annotations.summary: OS OOM killer invoked — process killed for memory

evidence: OOM kill: process=multi-agent-app pid=28471 killed. dmesg: 'Out of memory: Kill process 28471'. Free memory=0 Swap=0.
root_cause: OS-level OOM killer triggered (not K8s OOMKilled). Host memory exhausted across all cgroups.

verification_steps.rationale: OOM kill events in kernel log

proposed_remediation.step: Check total host memory vs pod/container limits; increase node memory or reduce workload density.

annotations.summary: Host swap fully consumed — severe memory pressure

evidence: remote_system_metrics: mem_pct=98.5 swap_pct=100. dmesg: 'kswapd: scan rate at maximum'. System thrashing.
root_cause: Host swap fully consumed. System is thrashing — excessive paging causing severe performance degradation.

verification_steps.rationale: OOM kill events in kernel log

proposed_remediation.step: Immediately identify largest memory consumers and reduce or evict; adding swap is not sufficient at this stage.

annotations.summary: Kernel OOPS / GPF — hardware or driver fault

evidence: dmesg probe: 'general protection fault' 'kernel BUG at' 'unable to handle kernel paging request'. Machine may be in unstable state.
root_cause: Kernel OOPS detected. System integrity is uncertain. Live migration or reboot required for safety.

verification_steps.rationale: OOM kill events in kernel log

proposed_remediation.step: Evacuate workloads, capture dmesg for RCA, schedule reboot during maintenance window.

annotations.summary: Network interface eth0 link DOWN

evidence: network probe: interface eth0 operstate=down carrier=0. `ip link show eth0` → state DOWN. All connectivity via this NIC lost.
root_cause: Physical or virtual NIC link is down. Cause: cable fault, switch port error, or VM NIC detached.

verification_steps.command: ip link show && ip addr show

proposed_remediation.step: Check physical/virtual switch port; `ip link set eth0 up`; if VM, verify NIC attachment in hypervisor.

annotations.summary: DNS resolution failing — NXDOMAIN / SERVFAIL

evidence: network probe: dns_resolve_time=timeout SERVFAIL for internal domains. `/etc/resolv.conf` points to unreachable nameserver.
root_cause: DNS resolver unreachable or misconfigured. All name-resolution-dependent services failing.

verification_steps.command: ip link show && ip addr show

proposed_remediation.step: Check /etc/resolv.conf nameservers; verify DNS server health; fallback to known-good resolver temporarily.

annotations.summary: TLS certificate expired — HTTPS handshake failing

evidence: network probe: certificate expired 3 days ago. `openssl s_client -connect api.internal:443` → Verify return code: 1 (unable to verify the first certificate). curl → SSL_ERROR_EXPIRED.
root_cause: TLS certificate for api.internal expired. All HTTPS clients failing handshake.

verification_steps.command: ip link show && ip addr show

proposed_remediation.step: Renew certificate immediately; if Let's Encrypt: certbot renew --force-renewal; reload nginx/haproxy after.

annotations.summary: Node NotReady due to kubelet or containerd crash

evidence: k8s_hard_fail probe: node=node-01 status=NotReady condition=KubeletNotReady. `systemctl status kubelet` → failed. `journalctl -u kubelet -n 50` → 'failed to run kubelet: unable to load bootstrap kubeconfig'.
root_cause: Kubelet process crashed or lost kubeconfig. Node is partitioned from control plane — all pods on node unschedulable.

verification_steps.rationale: Node condition detail from K8s API

proposed_remediation.step: Restart kubelet: systemctl restart kubelet; check kubeconfig exists and has valid credentials.

annotations.summary: containerd runtime crashed — pods unable to start

evidence: k8s_hard_fail probe: node=node-02. `systemctl status containerd` → failed. New pod creates failing: 'connection error: unable to connect to CRI runtime'. Existing pods running from cached state.
root_cause: Container runtime (containerd) crashed. New pods cannot be created; existing pods continue until restart.

verification_steps.rationale: Node condition detail from K8s API

proposed_remediation.step: systemctl restart containerd; if recurring, check /var/lib/containerd disk usage and /etc/containerd/config.toml.

annotations.summary: Node DiskPressure condition — kubelet evicting pods

evidence: k8s_hard_fail probe: node=node-03 DiskPressure=True. Kubelet evicting BestEffort pods. `df -h /var/lib/kubelet` → 97% full. imagefs also near capacity.
root_cause: Node disk pressure caused kubelet to set DiskPressure=True taint. BestEffort pods being evicted.

verification_steps.rationale: Node condition detail from K8s API

proposed_remediation.step: Free disk: docker image prune -f; crictl rmi --prune; check large log files in /var/log/pods.

annotations.summary: Node MemoryPressure — kubelet evicting pods

evidence: k8s_hard_fail probe: node=node-04 MemoryPressure=True available_memory=128Mi threshold=200Mi. Kubelet evicting pods. OOM killer active in kernel log.
root_cause: Node memory pressure: available memory below eviction threshold. Kubelet actively evicting pods.

verification_steps.rationale: Node condition detail from K8s API

proposed_remediation.step: Identify memory-heavy pods: kubectl top pods --all-namespaces --sort-by=memory | head -20; consider node cordon + drain.

annotations.summary: Daily backup cron job failed with exit code 1

evidence: cron_jobs probe: failed_cron_count=1 failed_jobs=['backup-daily'] last_exit_code=1. `journalctl -u cron -n 50` shows 'backup-daily exited with status 1'. Disk usage at destination: 99% — not enough space.
root_cause: Cron job backup-daily failed due to no space on destination volume.

proposed_remediation.step: df -h /backup; du -sh /backup/*; free space or move to another volume.

annotations.summary: Certificate renewal cron job stopped running

evidence: cron_jobs probe: failed_cron_count=0 but last_run_timestamp is 72h ago (expected every 24h). cert-renewal job entry exists in crontab but not in journalctl recent logs.
root_cause: Cron job silently stopped executing — cron daemon may have restarted without reloading crontab, or job is locked by a stale PID file.

proposed_remediation.step: Check cron daemon: systemctl status cron; verify crontab -l -u root; remove stale lockfile if present.

annotations.summary: Zombie process count exceeded threshold on node

evidence: zombie_processes probe: zombie_count=47 parent_pid=1234 parent_cmd='worker-pool'. `ps aux | grep Z` shows 47 zombie child processes. Parent not reaping children (no SIGCHLD handler).
root_cause: Worker pool parent process not calling wait() on child processes. Zombies accumulate until parent exits.

proposed_remediation.step: Send SIGHUP to parent: kill -HUP 1234; if process lacks proper SIGCHLD handler, restart the parent service.

annotations.summary: OOM killer terminated critical process

evidence: oom_events probe: oom_count=3 recent_oom_victims=['java-app-prod','java-app-prod','java-app-worker']. `dmesg | grep -i 'oom kill'` → 'Out of memory: Kill process 9821 (java) score 712 or sacrifice child'. Available memory at kill time: 42MB / 32GB.
root_cause: JVM heap limit not set; java-app allocated heap continuously until OOM killer intervened.

proposed_remediation.step: Set JVM heap: -Xmx8g -Xms2g; add memory limits in K8s PodSpec resources.limits.memory.

annotations.summary: OOM kill event affected kubelet process

evidence: oom_events probe: oom_count=1 recent_oom_victims=['kubelet']. Node entered NotReady state 30s after OOM kill. kubelet restarted via systemd watchdog after 60s.
root_cause: Kubelet process killed by OOM killer — insufficient node memory margin. System-level pods not protected from eviction.

proposed_remediation.step: Set kubelet as oom_score_adj=-999 via systemd override; ensure node allocatable memory reserves are set.

annotations.summary: RAID-5 array md1 degraded — one member disk failed

evidence: raid_mdadm probe: degraded_arrays=['md1'] failed_devices=1 active_devices=4 total_devices=5. `cat /proc/mdstat` → 'md1 : active raid5 sdb[0] sdc[1] sdd[2] sde[3] [5/4] [UUUU_]'. sdX device showing SMART errors: Reallocated_Sector_Ct=4096.
root_cause: One RAID-5 disk member failed SMART checks and was removed from array. Array in degraded mode — no redundancy.

proposed_remediation.step: Replace failed disk; add new disk: mdadm --add /dev/md1 /dev/sdX; monitor rebuild with watch cat /proc/mdstat.

annotations.summary: RAID-1 root array md0 failed — both mirrors unreadable

evidence: raid_mdadm probe: degraded_arrays=['md0'] failed_devices=2 array_state=inactive. `cat /proc/mdstat` → 'md0 : inactive sda[1](F) sdb[2](F)'. Both devices show I/O errors. Filesystem mounted read-only automatically.
root_cause: Both RAID-1 mirrors failed simultaneously — likely storage controller or backplane failure.

proposed_remediation.step: Boot from rescue media; fsck on surviving disk; contact hardware vendor — likely controller failure.

annotations.summary: LVM volume group vg_data in partial mode

evidence: lvm_volumes probe: partial_vgs=['vg_data'] failed_pvs=['/dev/sdc']. `vgs` → 'vg_data partial'. `pvs` → '/dev/sdc: MISSING'. Logical volumes on vg_data not mountable.
root_cause: Physical volume /dev/sdc missing from volume group. vg_data entered partial mode — data inaccessible.

proposed_remediation.step: vgchange -ay --partial vg_data; investigate /dev/sdc with smartctl; restore from backup if disk failed.

annotations.summary: Swap usage exceeds 90% — system memory critically low

evidence: swap_usage probe: swap_used_pct=94 swap_used=15.3GB swap_total=16GB. `free -m` → Swap: 16384 total, 15470 used, 914 free. `vmstat 1 5` → si=1240 so=890 (heavy swap I/O).
root_cause: System swapping heavily — insufficient RAM for workload. Performance severely degraded.

proposed_remediation.step: Identify top memory consumers: ps aux --sort=-%mem | head -20; kill non-critical processes; add RAM or reduce pod memory limits.

annotations.summary: Swap disabled but OOM events occurring

evidence: swap_usage probe: result=WARN swap_total=0 oom_events=5_last_hour. K8s cluster requires swap disabled; workloads exceed node RAM. `free -m` → Swap: 0 total, 0 used.
root_cause: No swap configured (correct for K8s) but workloads exceeding node RAM capacity without OOM protection.

proposed_remediation.step: Add memory resource limits to all pods; enable swap on non-K8s nodes or add node capacity.

annotations.summary: Physical network interface eth1 down

evidence: network_interfaces probe: down_interfaces=['eth1'] error_interfaces=[]. `ip link show eth1` → 'eth1: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST> mtu 1500 qdisc noop state DOWN'. ethtool eth1 → 'Link detected: no'.
root_cause: Physical NIC eth1 lost link — cable disconnected, switch port down, or NIC hardware failure.

verification_steps.command: dig +short kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local @$(kubectl get svc -n kube-system kube-dns -o jsonpath='{.spec.clusterIP}')

proposed_remediation.step: Check cable: ethtool eth1; test switch port; ip link set eth1 up; if persistent, replace NIC or cable.

annotations.summary: Bond interface reporting high TX/RX errors

evidence: network_interfaces probe: error_interfaces=['bond0'] tx_errors=12400 rx_errors=8900. `ip -s link show bond0` → RX errors 8900, TX errors 12400. One bond member (eth2) showing CRC errors via ethtool.
root_cause: Bond member eth2 experiencing hardware errors — faulty cable or NIC causing frame corruption.

verification_steps.command: dig +short kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local @$(kubectl get svc -n kube-system kube-dns -o jsonpath='{.spec.clusterIP}')

proposed_remediation.step: Identify bad member: ethtool eth2 | grep errors; ip link set eth2 nomaster; replace cable or NIC.

annotations.summary: DNS resolution failing for all queries from pods

evidence: dns_resolution probe: failed_lookups=['kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local','google.com'] lookup_error_count=847. `dig +short kubernetes.default @10.96.0.10` → ';; connection timed out'. CoreDNS pods Running but not responding.
root_cause: CoreDNS pods Running but TCP connections not reaching them — likely iptables/kube-proxy rules stale.

verification_steps.command: dig +short kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local @$(kubectl get svc -n kube-system kube-dns -o jsonpath='{.spec.clusterIP}')

proposed_remediation.step: Restart kube-proxy: kubectl rollout restart ds/kube-proxy -n kube-system; then restart CoreDNS: kubectl rollout restart deploy/coredns -n kube-system.

annotations.summary: DNS NXDOMAIN rate exceeds threshold — possible misconfiguration

evidence: dns_resolution probe: nxdomain_rate=1240_per_min lookup_error_count=0 nxdomain_domains=['db.legacy.svc']. Applications querying removed service 'db.legacy.svc'. CoreDNS logs: NXDOMAIN flood from namespace 'app-production'.
root_cause: Application pods configured with stale DNS name 'db.legacy.svc' that no longer exists. NXDOMAIN responses causing connection retry storms.

verification_steps.command: dig +short kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local @$(kubectl get svc -n kube-system kube-dns -o jsonpath='{.spec.clusterIP}')

proposed_remediation.step: Update app config: helm upgrade with correct service DNS name; CoreDNS rewrite plugin can stub the old name temporarily.

annotations.summary: TCP TIME_WAIT connections exceeding 50000

evidence: tcp_connections probe: time_wait_excess=True time_wait_count=62400 established=8900. `ss -s` → TIME-WAIT: 62400. `netstat -an | awk '{print $6}' | sort | uniq -c` confirms. Port exhaustion imminent: available ephemeral ports = 65535 - 62400 = 3135.
root_cause: Short-lived HTTP connections not reusing TCP sessions. tw_reuse disabled. Port exhaustion causes new connection failures.

verification_steps.command: dig +short kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local @$(kubectl get svc -n kube-system kube-dns -o jsonpath='{.spec.clusterIP}')

proposed_remediation.step: Enable TCP reuse: sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1; enable keepalive: sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time=60; implement HTTP keep-alive in application.

annotations.summary: SYN flood attack detected on port 443

evidence: tcp_connections probe: syn_flood_indicator=True syn_backlog_overflow=True port=443. `netstat -an | grep SYN_RECV | wc -l` → 4800. kernel: TCP: request_sock_TCP: Possible SYN flooding on port 443. Sending cookies.
root_cause: SYN flood attack on port 443. SYN cookies enabled but backlog exhausted.

verification_steps.command: dig +short kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local @$(kubectl get svc -n kube-system kube-dns -o jsonpath='{.spec.clusterIP}')

proposed_remediation.step: Enable SYN cookies: sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies=1; increase backlog: sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog=4096; add firewall rate-limit: iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --syn -m limit --limit 1/s -j ACCEPT.

annotations.summary: PostgreSQL replica lag exceeds 30s

evidence: postgresql_health probe: replication_lag_s=147 result=WARN replica_state=streaming. `SELECT * FROM pg_stat_replication` → replay_lag=00:02:27. Primary write rate: 45MB/s; replica network: 1Gbps saturated.
root_cause: Replica replication lag caused by network saturation. WAL shipping rate cannot keep up with write load.

verification_steps.command: redis-cli INFO replication; redis-cli INFO memory

proposed_remediation.step: Check wal_keep_size; increase network bandwidth or switch to logical replication with filtering; consider pglogical for selective replication.

annotations.summary: Redis instance using 95% of available OS memory

evidence: redis_os_health probe: result=WARN used_memory_human=14.8GB maxmemory=15GB eviction_policy=noeviction. `redis-cli INFO memory` → used_memory_peak=15845123328 maxmemory=16106127360. Eviction policy=noeviction → new writes will fail when limit reached.
root_cause: Redis approaching maxmemory limit with noeviction policy. New SET operations will return OOM error.

verification_steps.command: redis-cli INFO replication; redis-cli INFO memory

proposed_remediation.step: Change eviction policy: redis-cli CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru; or increase maxmemory: redis-cli CONFIG SET maxmemory 24gb.

annotations.summary: MongoDB replica set secondary is 120s behind primary

evidence: mongodb_health probe: repl_lag_s=120 result=WARN rs_state=SECONDARY oplog_lag=PT2M. `db.adminCommand('replSetGetStatus')` → members[1].optimeDate is 2 minutes behind primary. oplog window: 24h — not at risk of falling off.
root_cause: MongoDB secondary replication lag 120s — likely caused by heavy writes to primary exceeding secondary apply throughput.

verification_steps.command: redis-cli INFO replication; redis-cli INFO memory

proposed_remediation.step: Check secondary resources: db.serverStatus().opcounters; if CPU-bound, scale secondary instance; review write concern w:majority impact.

annotations.summary: Machine Check Exception (MCE) detected — hardware error

evidence: kernel_errors probe: critical_errors=['MCE: PROCESSOR 0:906EA BANK 5'] mce_count=12. `dmesg -T | grep -i mce` → 'mce: [Hardware Error]: Machine check events logged'. `mcelog --client` → 'MEMORY CONTROLLER RD_CHANNEL0_ERR'. Memory controller error bank 5.
root_cause: Hardware MCE on memory controller channel 0. DIMM in slot A1 likely failing. Correctable ECC errors accumulating — may progress to uncorrectable.

verification_steps.rationale: ECC error counters via EDAC or IPMI

proposed_remediation.step: Schedule node drain: kubectl drain node-05 --ignore-daemonsets; replace DIMM in slot A1; run memtest86+ before returning to service.

annotations.summary: Kernel I/O errors on storage device /dev/sdb

evidence: kernel_errors probe: critical_errors=['blk_update_request: I/O error, dev sdb'] mce_count=0. `dmesg -T | grep sdb` → 'end_request: I/O error, dev sdb, sector 4096000'. SMART: Reallocated_Sector_Ct=8192 Offline_Uncorrectable=47.
root_cause: SATA disk /dev/sdb experiencing hardware failures. 47 offline uncorrectable sectors. Data loss risk if disk not replaced immediately.

verification_steps.rationale: ECC error counters via EDAC or IPMI

proposed_remediation.step: Set disk offline: echo offline > /sys/block/sdb/device/state; if RAID member: mdadm --fail /dev/mdX /dev/sdb; schedule disk replacement.

annotations.summary: ECC correctable memory errors exceeding threshold

evidence: memory_hw_errors probe: correctable_errors=2847 uncorrectable_errors=0 dimm_slot='A2'. `edac-util -s` → 'mc0: 2847 Corrected Errors'. `ipmitool sel list` → 'Memory ECC correctable error DIMM_A2 count=2847'.
root_cause: DIMM A2 experiencing high correctable ECC error rate — hardware degradation, not yet causing data corruption but likely to progress to uncorrectable.

verification_steps.rationale: ECC error counters via EDAC or IPMI

proposed_remediation.step: Drain and schedule maintenance: kubectl drain node-07; replace DIMM A2 slot; monitor post-replacement: edac-util -s for 24h.

annotations.summary: ECC uncorrectable memory error — system panic imminent

evidence: memory_hw_errors probe: correctable_errors=0 uncorrectable_errors=3 result=FAILED. `dmesg -T | grep -i 'uncorrectable'` → 'EDAC MC0: 3 UE errors on mc#0csrow#1channel#0'. System has already panic-reset twice in last 4 hours.
root_cause: Uncorrectable ECC errors — DIMM hardware failure causing data corruption. System panic loop will continue until DIMM replaced.

verification_steps.rationale: ECC error counters via EDAC or IPMI

proposed_remediation.step: Immediate action: kubectl drain --force node-08; power off node; replace DIMM; do NOT restart without hardware fix — data corruption risk.

annotations.summary: RAID controller reporting critical error

evidence: kernel_errors probe: critical_errors=['megaraid_sas: FAILED to init firmware'] mce_count=0. `dmesg | grep megaraid` → 'megaraid_sas 0000:03:00.0: FW fault state detected'. All RAID volumes offline. Boot to BIOS reports controller in fault state.
root_cause: MegaRAID controller firmware fault. All volumes hosted on this controller are offline.

verification_steps.rationale: ECC error counters via EDAC or IPMI

proposed_remediation.step: Boot from recovery media; check controller battery backup; try firmware reset via CTRL+R at boot; contact vendor support — possible controller hardware failure.

annotations.summary: Docker daemon crashed — container operations failing

evidence: docker_daemon probe: daemon_error='connection refused' unhealthy_containers=0. `systemctl status docker` → 'Active: failed (Result: exit-code)'. `journalctl -u docker -n 30` → 'failed to start daemon: error initializing graphdriver: overlay2: failed to Mount'.  /var/lib/docker filesystem 100% full.
root_cause: Docker daemon failed to start because overlay2 storage driver mount failed — disk full.

verification_steps.command: docker system df; docker ps --filter health=unhealthy
verification_steps.rationale: Docker disk usage and unhealthy containers

proposed_remediation.step: Free disk space: docker system prune -f; journalctl --vacuum-size=1G; then: systemctl start docker.

annotations.summary: Multiple Docker containers in unhealthy state

evidence: docker_daemon probe: daemon_error=None unhealthy_containers=8. `docker ps --filter health=unhealthy` → 8 containers in unhealthy state. HEALTHCHECK commands timing out: 'health: maximum consecutive failures exceeded'.
root_cause: 8 containers failing their configured HEALTHCHECK probes. Likely backend services they depend on are down (database, cache).

verification_steps.command: docker system df; docker ps --filter health=unhealthy
verification_steps.rationale: Docker disk usage and unhealthy containers

proposed_remediation.step: docker inspect <container_id> | jq '.[0].State.Health'; identify failing healthcheck command; fix dependency or tune healthcheck timeout.

annotations.summary: containerd entering crash loop — pod creates failing

evidence: containerd_state probe: daemon_error='rpc error: code=Unavailable' plugin_errors=['io.containerd.snapshotter.v1.overlayfs']. `systemctl status containerd` → 'activating (start) / start-pre'. overlayfs snapshotter plugin failing to initialize — /var/lib/containerd 98% full.
root_cause: containerd snapshotter plugin failing because /var/lib/containerd storage is nearly full. New image pulls and container creates fail.

verification_steps.command: docker system df; docker ps --filter health=unhealthy
verification_steps.rationale: Docker disk usage and unhealthy containers

proposed_remediation.step: Free space: crictl rmi --prune; find /var/lib/containerd -name '*.img' -mtime +7 -delete; systemctl restart containerd.

annotations.summary: containerd CNI plugin error — pod networking broken

evidence: containerd_state probe: daemon_error=None plugin_errors=['cni-bridge: failed to set bridge addr']. `journalctl -u containerd -n 30` → 'CNI failed to setup network for sandbox: failed to set bridge addr: bridge with same IP already exists'. New pods stuck in ContainerCreating.
root_cause: CNI bridge plugin conflict — existing bridge interface has same IP as new pod CIDR assignment. Stale CNI state from previous pod network teardown.

verification_steps.command: docker system df; docker ps --filter health=unhealthy
verification_steps.rationale: Docker disk usage and unhealthy containers

proposed_remediation.step: Clean stale CNI state: rm -rf /var/lib/cni/networks/bridge/*; ip link delete cni0 2>/dev/null; ip link delete flannel.1 2>/dev/null; systemctl restart containerd kubelet.

annotations.summary: Docker container storage quota exceeded

evidence: docker_daemon probe: daemon_error=None unhealthy_containers=3 disk_usage_pct=97. `docker system df` → Images: 45.2GB, Containers: 12.1GB, Local Volumes: 8.9GB, Build Cache: 22.4GB. New container creates failing: 'no space left on device'.
root_cause: Docker build cache and stopped container layers consuming 88GB+. No automatic cleanup configured.

verification_steps.command: docker system df; docker ps --filter health=unhealthy
verification_steps.rationale: Docker disk usage and unhealthy containers

proposed_remediation.step: docker system prune --volumes -f; add cronjob: 0 3 * * * /usr/bin/docker system prune -f --filter 'until=168h'; set daemon.json: {"log-opts":{"max-size":"10m","max-file":"3"}}.

annotations.summary: Nginx upstream group fully down — all backends offline

evidence: service_nginx probe: error_rate_pct=100 upstream_errors=['upstream timed out (110)','no live upstreams']. `nginx -t` → 'syntax is ok'. `curl -I localhost` → 502 Bad Gateway. upstream group 'app_backend' has 0 of 5 servers responding.
root_cause: All upstream application servers in app_backend group are offline or not responding. Nginx returning 502 to all requests.

proposed_remediation.step: Check upstream health: curl http://app-server-01:8080/health; kubectl get pods -l app=backend -n production; if pods Running, check service selector and endpoint: kubectl get endpoints backend-svc.

annotations.summary: Nginx configuration reload failed after ConfigMap change

evidence: service_nginx probe: result=FAILED daemon_error='nginx: configuration file test failed'. `nginx -t` → 'nginx: [emerg] unknown directive "proxy_set_headerr" in /etc/nginx/conf.d/app.conf:14'. Typo in directive name introduced by recent ConfigMap update.
root_cause: Nginx configuration contains typo 'proxy_set_headerr'. Config test failed; nginx reload rejected — currently serving with previous (good) config.

proposed_remediation.step: Fix ConfigMap typo; apply: kubectl apply -f nginx-cm.yaml; exec into pod: nginx -t; if OK: nginx -s reload.

annotations.summary: VRRP failover occurred — VIP moved to backup node

evidence: service_keepalived probe: result=WARN state=BACKUP vip_assigned_to='node-02' was_master=True. `journalctl -u keepalived` → 'Transition to BACKUP state'. node-01 network interface flap detected 120s before state change.
root_cause: Keepalived master node-01 lost VRRP advertisement due to network interface flap. node-02 (backup) correctly assumed MASTER role. VIP functional on node-02.

proposed_remediation.step: Verify VIP: ip addr show | grep <VIP>; ping <VIP>; investigate node-01 NIC: ethtool eth0 | grep 'Link detected'; if stable, manually preempt back: systemctl restart keepalived on node-01.
